rows.what_the_ink_shows: Full scan inspected first. crops/62_scan093_L828_J_order.png shows J(i) first and J(1/2+i sqrt(3)/2) second. crops/62_scan093_L828_values_and_invariants.png shows the subsequent order 0 et 1, followed by g_2=0 et g_3=0; the parenthesis repeats g_2=0 before g_3=0. The 0 is a loop and the 1 a single upright stroke; the g subscripts visibly distinguish the bent 2 from the double-curved 3. crops/62_scan093_L828_ratios.png shows i as the first stated ratio and the second ratio beginning with a fraction plus i sqrt(3)/2. The small lower denominator already marked uncertain in the LaTeX is not used to infer a different order.
rows.note: The proposed reversal is an author-slip correction: the actual order 0 then 1 and g_2=0 then g_3=0 matches the original transcription and is retained. The supplied correction gives intended J(i)=1 with g_3=0, and J(1/2+i sqrt(3)/2)=0 with g_2=0, citing lattice symmetries and J=g_2^3/Delta; these mathematical statements were not independently proved here. The supplied paraphrase presents the lower real-part denominator as 2, whereas the original LaTeX has \frac1{\unsure{2|3}}; that existing uncertainty is preserved. No text or annotation is changed.
